items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: is not the run-of-the-mill Irving Berlin song

ctx.x: Well, the door was open. I seen she went across the street to... You had to look at her twice because she was such a fine young girl, and to see that... You know, to hear her involved in something like that... So later on I go across to Pa and Jerry's, because they was tellin' me about the Lion, and I went over there and I seen her in there. And she was waiting tables, and later on she sang. So there was... Tommy Dorsey, Jimmy Dorsey, Bert Lom, Paul Whiteman, everybody, all the White musicians used to go to Pa…

And they had this upstairs, too, but it was a little crowded place, and it would get real smoky quick. And there was Willie Smith, the Lion, playing piano, playing his versions that was ahead of time. Like his things, "Morning Air" and all them pretty things he'd play at intermission, was constructed in a manner that it's not the run-of-the-mill Irving Berlin song. This thing is all intricate, and you don't even sit down with him if you don't know what
